name: split-flap-text
title: Split Flap Text
description: A split-flap board that scrambles its letter tiles and settles on a new line each cycle, styled like an airport departures sign. Words, timing and tile styling are configurable.
use: A headline or status line should feel mechanical and retro, cycling through several short messages.
avoid: Every tile runs its own flip loop, which is busy and hard to read for anyone sensitive to motion.
a11y: The current phrase is exposed as one text label while the scrambling tiles are hidden from assistive tech. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: Rows of small dark rounded tiles each hold one pale monospace capital, split by a faint hinge line across the middle. Sparse uppercase captions sit above and below the board on a black surface.
behaves: Every character cycles through random glyphs before settling on its target, cascading left to right, then the board holds and moves to the next phrase on a loop.
customise: Words or a text string, flip duration, stagger, cycle delay, charset, flips per char, tile and text colours, sizes, alignment and tile style are props.
weight: moderate: A rAF loop drives up to a dozen tiles through several flips every cycle.
demo: Departure phrases LISBON 09:45, BERLIN 10:20, TOKYO 11:05 and NEW YORK 12:30 under 'Departures, Terminal 2'.
issues: The tiles spend most of each cycle showing random letters, so a quick screenshot can look like gibberish.
polishWhy: Convincing flap shading and a crisp monospace board; the scramble only reads at rest.
